About the Scholarship

The UK Government's global scholarship programme offering fully funded one-year taught Master's degrees at UK universities.

OpportunityFully Funded Scholarship: Chevening Scholarships (UK Government)
HostUK Government
LocationVarious, United Kingdom
Study LevelMaster's
FundingFully Funded
StipendFull tuition + monthly stipend + airfare + visa & travel
Application Deadline6 October 2026
ApplyOfficial application page ↗

Funding detail: Full tuition + monthly stipend + airfare + visa & travel allowances.

Basic Information

  • Host Institution: Various UK Universities
  • Study Level: Master's (One-year taught)
  • Funding Type: Fully Funded
  • Coverage: Full tuition, monthly stipend, travel expenses (~£51,920 total)
  • Eligibility: Global program for future leaders
  • Application Period: 4 August – 6 October 2026

Project Overview & Significance

Chevening is the UK Government's international scholarships programme, funded by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) and partner organisations. It offers a unique opportunity for outstanding emerging leaders from over 160 countries to pursue a fully funded one-year Master's degree at any UK university. The programme is not just about academic funding; it is a leadership development initiative designed to build a global network of 'Chevening Alumni' who are committed to driving positive change in their home countries. By providing full financial support—covering tuition, living expenses, and travel—the scholarship ensures that financial barriers do not prevent top talent from accessing world-class UK education. Chevening Scholars are selected not only for their academic excellence but for their leadership potential, networking skills, and a clear vision for how a UK Master's will help them drive progress in their respective fields.

Research Themes & Objectives

There are no specific research themes, as the scholarship is open to all academic subjects. However, applicants must demonstrate how their chosen Master's programme aligns with their career goals and how they intend to use their UK education to contribute to their home country's development. Whether studying public policy, engineering, business, or the arts, the objective is to equip scholars with the knowledge, skills, and networks needed to become influential leaders and decision-makers.

Training & Development

Beyond the academic degree itself, Chevening offers a unparalleled professional and cultural development programme. Scholars become part of a highly engaged, global alumni network. The programme includes exclusive networking events, policy seminars, and professional placements. The experience of living and studying in the UK for a year builds cross-cultural understanding and access to the UK's leading institutions, think tanks, and businesses. Chevening Alumni go on to become prime ministers, Nobel laureates, and leaders of major NGOs and corporations.

Eligibility and Requirements

Applicants must be a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country. They must have completed an undergraduate degree equivalent to at least an upper second-class 2:1 honours degree in the UK. Crucially, applicants must have at least two years of work experience (or 2,400 hours) and demonstrate leadership potential. They must also meet the Chevening English language requirement.

How to Apply & Official Contacts

Applications open in August and close in early November each year. Candidates must apply via the official Chevening website. The application process is rigorous, involving an online application, reference letters, and, if shortlisted, an interview at the British Embassy or High Commission in the applicant's home country.

Official Link

https://www.chevening.org/

Important Notes

  • Always confirm the full requirements and current deadline on the official website before applying.
  • Prepare the requested documents early — competitive awards are often decided on complete, on-time submissions.
  • Funding terms shown here reflect the listing at the time of publication and can be updated by the provider.
